messages:
Evan (AE): Quick sync — here's a short writeup from last night's perf run with NovaHealth POC.
Evan (AE): Results and obs in the GCS summary: gs://redwood-poc/novahealth/2026-03-21/summary.pdf
Priya (Eng-Perf): Saw a clear latency cliff once concurrent requests hit ~80 per shard. Median stable, p95 and p99 spike. Raw numbers below.
Priya (Eng-Perf): Test command used:
```
rwt-load --model redwood-v2-13b --concurrency 160 --qps 500 --seq 1024 --workload synth-chat
```
Devon (Solutions): What was request mix? chat vs rerank vs embeddings? Was KV cache warm?
Evan (AE): Mix ~85% chat (system+user), 15% rerank. KV cache warm (we primed with 2k prefixes). Warmup 10m.
Priya (Eng-Perf): Numbers:
- QPS: 500 sustained
- median latency: 52ms
- p95: 220ms
- p99: 510ms
- GPU util (per card): 62-88% (spikes during bursts)
- avg batch size: 18 (dynamic batching)
Priya (Eng-Perf): Hypothesis: dynamic batching+auto-batching threshold causes queueing at higher concurrency; large batches reduce per-token cost but increase tail latency.
Devon (Solutions): Can we pin batch size / reduce max latency by forcing smaller batches? Any cost impact?
Priya (Eng-Perf): Quick experiment:
```
rwt-load --model redwood-v2-13b --concurrency 160 --qps 500 --max-batch 8
```
Result: p95 dropped to ~140ms, p99 ~280ms. Token cost increased ~+11% (less batching efficiency), throughput steady.
Ryan (Sales-Eng): Pricing Q: for customer POC we discussed reserved vs on-demand. If they want consistent p95<200ms we'd recommend Dedicated (2xA10g equiv). Rough ballpark commit for their expected QPS (500) is ~$20k/mo. That's a rough estimate, we should firm up with finance.
Carla (Security): Enterprise blocker: NovaHealth legal insists on IP allowlist, audit logs retention 1 year, and support for KMS in our Private offering. Also need answers to several questionnaire items around data residency.
Evan (AE): Noted. Priya — can Dedicated/Private cover these? Any technical caveats for the Dedicated config used in the perf run?
Priya (Eng-Perf): Yes — Dedicated can be deployed in their VPC or our Private package for on-prem. Both support KMS/HSM for keys and audit logs. The runtime already emits per-request trace IDs (we can ship logs to their SIEM). I'll post the security checklist link.
Priya (Eng-Perf): Security checklist: https://redwood.internal/sec/pocs/novahealth (internal link)
Carla (Security): Thanks. Also ask: do we have an SLA for p95? For POC we can make best-effort, but enterprise asks for SLOs on Dedicated tiers.
Devon (Solutions): Operational recommendation: run the regression test in their morning (US East) for 2 hours, collect traces, and run a canary with max-batch 8 for latency-critical routes, and allow batch 18 for throughput routes.
Evan (AE): Action items:
- Priya: run 2h regression with pinned max-batch 8 and upload logs (assigned) — target: tomorrow 09:00 ET
- Devon: prepare updated cost estimate and call out tradeoffs for the account
- Carla: start security questionnaire with NovaHealth contacts
- Ryan: include ~20k/mo reserved example in next pricing doc, flag as provisional
Evan (AE): Any objections? :thumbsup:
Priya (Eng-Perf): LGTM. I'll drop the logs and a short script to reproduce.
load-bot: Load test finished: run_id=run-184500-01 status=complete artifacts=gs://redwood-poc/novahealth/2026-03-21/run-01
Evan (AE): Great, let's sync tomorrow morning. Thanks everyone.
Carla (Security): Noted, will ping legal and infra. 
Ryan (Sales-Eng): I'll queue a follow-up with their CTO to confirm preferred deployment model.
Evan (AE): Closing notes: if we need lower p99 we should consider model quantization + dedicated 4-card pools; raises cost but better tails.
Priya (Eng-Perf): Agreed — can prepare perf/cost delta for quantized 8-bit variant.
Evan (AE): End thread.
